source.title: Dromore Leader, 21 May 1949, p. 3 ("Nominations for Down County Council"); Banbridge Chronicle, 21 May 1949, p. 3 ("Banbridge Rural Council: 20 divisions, 14 nominations"); Banbridge Chronicle, 4 June 1949, p. 2 ("Notice of result of elections: Rural District of Banbridge, election of rural district councillors, 1949 (dated 2 June 1949)")
source.publisher: Dromore Leader (via the British Newspaper Archive)

note: Triennial election of the 20 electoral divisions of Banbridge rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. Nominations were received on 17 May: fourteen divisions were filled unopposed, and no nomination was received for Balloolymore, Ballybrick, Ballyward, Leitrim, Skeagh or Tullylish. The returning officer's notice of result (Banbridge Chronicle, 4 June 1949, p. 2) enters the retiring members for Balloolymore, Ballybrick, Ballyward, Skeagh and Tullylish as deemed to be re-elected (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Leitrim is not in the notice at all: with no nomination and no retiring member deemed re-elected, the seat stood vacant until the next ordinary election (S.R.&O. 1949 No. 18, reg. 15(1)); Owen M'Elroy was returned for it in 1952. New member. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
